# Tax Directives API

SARS tax directive handling — lump sum / retirement / severance / death payments. A directive is a SARS-issued document that specifies the tax rate to apply to an irregular payment. This module tracks directives AND applies them to actual payroll payments.

Services: `src/modules/accounting/services/payroll/taxDirectiveService.ts` (CRUD) and `taxDirectivePaymentService.ts` (apply → journal).

## Endpoints

| Method + path | Handler | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/accounting/tax-directives` | `index.ts` | List directives. Filters: `?status=pending\|approved\|expired\|cancelled`, `?search=` (matches employee_name). |
| `POST /api/accounting/tax-directives` | `index.ts` | Create directive. `employee_id` is REQUIRED and must be one of the company's payroll employees (400 otherwise, before any write). The employee must be `active` or `terminated` (an `inactive` one is 400). `employee_name` is ALWAYS the employee record's (a body value is ignored: it could name someone else); `employee_tax_number` is ALWAYS the record's too, NULL when the record has none (a body value is ignored, decided 2026-10-24: the certificate's 3150 reads the record); a non-string text field is 400 (`employee_name` / `employee_tax_number` are ignored, so not checked); `amount` / `tax_rate` must be a number or a numeric string (an array was coerced). The form shows the name and tax number read-only. Body: `{ employee_id, employee_name, employee_tax_number?, directive_number?, directive_type: 'lump_sum'\|'retirement'\|'severance'\|'death', amount, tax_rate (decimal fraction, e.g. 0.18), effective_date, issued_date? (YYYY-MM-DD, the SARS issue date, e@syFile 3231), expiry_date?, sars_reference?, notes? }`. |
| `GET /api/accounting/tax-directives/[id]` | `[id].ts` | Single directive. |
| `PATCH /api/accounting/tax-directives/[id]` | `[id].ts` | Update `status` and/or `issued_date` (or null). `employee_id` cannot be changed (400): the run's claim at approval does not re-read the employee, so moving an approved directive would let a run calculated for the first employee claim it; cancel and create anew. A directive whose payment stands (run claim or stand-alone, while its journal is in force) cannot leave `approved`: **409** naming what paid it; reverse that journal first. |
| `DELETE /api/accounting/tax-directives/[id]` | `[id].ts` | Delete directive. **409** while it is paid (the paid guard) or any payment row names it; cancel it instead. |
| `POST /api/accounting/tax-directives/[id]/apply` | `[id]/apply.ts` | **Apply** the directive — creates a `tax_directive_payments` row + posts GL journal. Body: `{ paymentDate: YYYY-MM-DD, bankAccountId?: uuid }`. UNIQUE per directive — second call throws "already applied". |

## Auth

All routes wrap `withAuth(withErrorHandler(withCsrf(withWriteAccess(handler))))`. UUID guard on `[id]` returns `notFound` for non-UUID ids.

## Response contract

`apiResponse.success` / `.created` / `.badRequest` / `.notFound`. Clients unwrap `json.data`.

## Apply-flow journal

```
DR 5200 Labour Costs       = directive.amount          (gross expense)
CR 2140 PAYE Payable       = amount × tax_rate         (paye owed to SARS)
CR 1110 Bank (or override) = amount − paye             (net to employee)
```

Cent-level balance guard — throws before creating the entry if the arithmetic doesn't round.

## Tables

- `tax_directives` (mig 310) — the directive record. `status` values: `pending | approved | expired | cancelled`. Note: no `paid` status — applied directives stay `approved` and link via `tax_directive_payments`.
- `tax_directive_payments` (mig 403) — one row per applied directive (UNIQUE constraint on `(company_id, tax_directive_id)`). FK to `gl_journal_entries.id` via `journal_entry_id`.

## Gotchas

- **`tax_rate` is stored as a decimal fraction**, not a percentage. `0.18` = 18%. The lump-sum calculator component in `src/components/payroll/TaxDirectiveComponents.tsx` converts the user input (percentage) to fraction on submit.
- **Only `approved` directives can be applied** — `applyTaxDirective` guards status (409 otherwise) and requires `employee_id` to be a payroll employee of the company (400): the payment goes on that employee's IRP5. Create a directive first, PATCH to `approved`, then POST `/apply`.
- The form in `TaxDirectiveComponents.tsx` has a required employee select (PAYE 4a follow-ups round 2, R4), fed by `GET /api/payroll/employees?include=terminated` (leavers included: severance, retirement and death directives are for people who have left); picking fills `employee_name` and `employee_tax_number`, both read-only. Directives made by the old form have no employee: cancel and re-create them. Tests: `tests/integration/p4fu-r2b-directive-employee.int.test.ts`, `tests/unit/components/taxDirectiveEmployeePicker.test.tsx`.
- **`tax_directive_payments` needs a `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON tax_directive_payments TO app_user`** — the mig was initially deployed without grants. Apply API 500'd until granted.
- **Modal in `TaxDirectiveComponents.tsx` POSTs to `/api/accounting/tax-directives`** (create). "Apply" is a separate button on the list row that POSTs to `/:id/apply`.
